title: Job Appraisal Interview
summary: We read an appraisal report about Emma and talked about her strengths and weaknesses at work. We used could, may, might and should to give polite recommendations, and practised giving positive and negative feedback on someone's work.

grammar.title: Modal verbs for recommendations (could, may, might, should)
grammar.explain: In the appraisal report, the writer uses could, may, might and should to give recommendations, not orders. They talk about the future. 'Should' is stronger; 'could', 'may' and 'might' are softer and more polite. After a modal verb we use the base form of the verb.
grammar.explain_ar: في تقرير التقييم يستخدم الكاتب could وmay وmight وshould لتقديم توصيات واقتراحات وليس أوامر إلزامية، وهي تتحدث عن المستقبل. should أقوى في النصيحة، أما could وmay وmight فهي ألطف وأكثر تهذيباً. بعد الفعل الناقص نستخدم المصدر بدون to وبدون s.
form: subject + could / may / might / should + base verb: Emma could continue working in this area.
One possibility might be (for her) + to + verb: One possibility might be for her to attend time management courses.
A good idea may be + to + verb: A good idea may be to lead a series of seminars.
should = stronger advice; could / may / might = softer, more polite suggestions

examples.en: Emma should ensure that her meetings start and end on time.
Emma could discuss her ways of approaching customers with our customer service managers.
examples.note: A possible idea for the future.

examples.en: Emma might need to work on her creativity.
examples.note: A soft, polite way to talk about a weakness.

examples.en: Anna has problems sleeping. She could try sleeping pills.
Alexander wants to sell his flat. He might try advertising online.
Your friend doesn't know what to buy. You could always go with flowers.

mistakes.wrong: She should to attend a course.
mistakes.why: No 'to' after could, may, might or should.
No -s on the verb after a modal.

mistakes.right: He should work on his creativity.
mistakes.why: We 'work on' a skill we want to improve.

quiz.q: Emma should ___ that her meetings start on time.
Maria can't give up smoking. She ___ go on a special course.
Which sentence is a polite recommendation, not an order?
options: Take it to a mechanic now!
You could take it to a mechanic.
You must take it to a mechanic.

quiz.q: Kira hasn't got enough money for a flat. She could ___ the bank for a loan.
Which modal gives the strongest advice?

quiz.why: We say 'work on' something to improve it.

grammar.title: Present perfect for something still true now (for / since)
grammar.explain: If someone started a job in the past and still does it now, use the present perfect (has/have + past participle) with for or since. The past simple means the situation is finished.
grammar.explain_ar: إذا بدأ شخص عملاً في الماضي وما زال يقوم به الآن نستخدم المضارع التام (has/have + التصريف الثالث للفعل) مع for للمدة أو since لنقطة البداية. أما الماضي البسيط فيعني أن الأمر انتهى.
form: has / have + past participle + for + a period of time: He has worked in this position for 2 years.
has / have + past participle + since + a starting point: She has worked here since 2023.
has / have been + -ing (to show a continuing activity): Emma has been working for the company for 3 years.

examples.en: He has worked in this position for 2 years.
He worked in this position for 2 years.
examples.note: Finished: he doesn't work there now.

examples.en: Emma has been working for the company for 3 years.
examples.note: From the handout: she still works there.

mistakes.wrong: He worked in this position for 2 years. (He still works there.)
mistakes.right: He has worked in this position for 2 years.

mistakes.wrong: I work here for two years.
mistakes.right: I have worked here for two years.
mistakes.why: Use the present perfect with 'for' when it is still true now.

quiz.q: He ___ in this position for 2 years, and he still loves it.
quiz.why: He still works there → present perfect.

quiz.q: My father ___ in a bank for ten years, but now he's retired.
quiz.why: It is finished, so use the past simple.

quiz.q: We have known each other ___ years.

phrases.en: Over the next year, Emma could continue working in this area.
Emma should ensure that her meetings start and end on time.
One possibility might be for her to attend time management courses.
One of the ways for Emma to advance next year could be to cooperate with other departments.
A good idea for Emma's development next year may be to lead a series of seminars.
Emma might need to work on her creativity.
She is good at altering course when it is required.
One of her most important skills is her ability to communicate on complex topics.
One of the positives about her management style is her ability to build unity.
On the other hand, she leads meetings which often run beyond their allocated time.
phrases.use: Moving from a strength to a weakness
